main.title: PUBG
main.subtitle: Track detailed PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS stats and leaderboards

about.h1: PUBG stats tracker for Steam, Xbox and PlayStation
about.lead: Type a nickname into the box above and you get that player's current season: ranked RP and tier, kills and damage, win rate, and the last matches they played — each one openable as a replay. Everything comes from the official PUBG API, and nothing here needs an account.

lookup.heading: Three ways to find a player
lookup.p1: The quickest is the in-game nickname. It is case-sensitive and it is the name as it is written today, so a player who renamed since you last saw them will not come up under the old one — PUBG keeps no alias history and neither can we.
lookup.p2: You can also paste a Steam profile URL, in either the vanity form or the numeric one, and we resolve it to the PUBG account behind it. And if you already have an account ID, the kind that starts with account. and a long string of hex, that works too and skips the lookup entirely.

platforms.heading: Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Kakao and Stadia
platforms.p1: Pick the platform before you search. PUBG keeps a separate account and separate statistics per platform, so the same nickname can belong to two different people on Steam and Xbox, and a console player will not be found on the Steam shard no matter how the name is spelled.
platforms.p2: Kakao is its own region rather than a platform in the usual sense: it runs on a separate shard with its own ranked ladder and its own Survivor slots. Stadia is still addressable in the API even though the service is gone, which is why the option remains.

playerPage.heading: What a player page shows
playerPage.p1: The season view carries K/D, win rate, average damage, longest kill, headshot percentage, top 10 finishes and time played, split by game mode. Beside it sits the ranked picture: current RP, the tier that RP puts the player in, and where that stands against everyone else on the ladder.
playerPage.p2: Under it are the recent matches, and each one opens as a replay: where every squad dropped, how the blue zone closed, the kill feed in order, and the point on the map where each player was eliminated. Survival and weapon mastery, the clan and the Steam avatar load beside all of it.

ranked.heading: Ranked, RP and where you stand
ranked.p1: Since Season 36 there is a single RP number rather than one per party type and perspective, so the tier on a profile is the tier for everything the player queues. Eight tiers run from Bronze to Survivor, and the top one needs both an RP threshold and a slot in its region.
ranked.p2: RP alone does not tell you much without knowing what the ladder looks like, which is what the two pages below are for.

data.heading: Where the numbers come from
data.p1: Everything on this site is read from KRAFTON's official PUBG API. Matches stay available there for about fourteen days, so match history is a recent window rather than a career archive, and older matches simply stop being fetchable.
data.p2: An empty profile is usually one of three things: the player has not played the current season, the platform is wrong, or the API is rate-limiting us and we are serving the last good copy while the limit clears. When that happens the page says so rather than showing zeroes as if they were real.

about.lead: This is the top 500 by rank points for one region and one game mode, read from the official PUBG API for the season selected above. Change either selector and you get a different 500.

ladders.heading: Each region and mode is its own board
ladders.p1: RP is a single number per account, but the board is cut per region and per mode. A player near the top of one list can be absent from another entirely, because that is simply not the queue they play.
ladders.p2: Survivor, the tier above Master, is capped per region rather than by RP alone: it needs 3,700 RP and a seat, and the seats are finite. So the very top of two regions' boards need not sit at the same RP.

rpNotWins.heading: Ordered by RP, not by win rate
rpNotWins.p1: Rank points reward placement and consistency as much as kills. A player can sit high here with a win rate that looks ordinary, and a player who wins spectacularly in short bursts can be missing from the board altogether.
rpNotWins.p2: So read the columns beside RP as description rather than as the ranking: they are that player's season, not the reason they hold this position.

scope.heading: What the top 500 does not tell you
scope.p1: This is the top of the ladder and nothing else — five hundred names out of a ranked population that starts at Bronze. Nothing on this page says where a typical player sits, and a leaderboard never can.
scope.p2: That question has an answer of its own: the ranks page carries a measured tier distribution, sampled from ranked matches rather than read off this board.

data.heading: Where these numbers come from
data.p1: Everything here is read from KRAFTON's official PUBG API. The time beside the table is when this copy of the board was fetched, not when PUBG last recalculated it.
data.p2: Ranked resets every season, so a board from a finished season is a record of that season and not a statement about the ladder now.

help.subtitle: Short answers to the questions we get most: finding a player, reading the numbers, and what to do when a profile will not load.

search.q: How do I look up a PUBG player?
search.a: Pick the platform first, then type the in-game nickname into the box on the home page. The name is case-sensitive and it has to be the name the player uses today: PUBG keeps no record of previous nicknames, so an account that was renamed will not come up under the old one. A Steam profile URL works too, in either the vanity or the numeric form, and so does an account ID beginning with “account.”, which skips the lookup entirely.

platforms.a: Steam, Xbox, PlayStation, Kakao and Stadia. PUBG keeps a separate account and separate statistics per platform, so the same nickname can belong to two different people on Steam and Xbox, and a console player will never be found on the Steam shard however the name is spelled. Kakao is its own region rather than a platform in the usual sense: separate shard, separate ranked ladder, separate Survivor slots. Stadia is still addressable in the API even though the service is gone, which is why the option remains.

season.q: Which season am I looking at?
season.a: The current one, unless you change it. Ranked resets every season, so a tier and an RP number only mean something next to the season they were earned in — the dropdown on a player page switches between the seasons the API still holds.

history.q: Why can I not see my older matches?
history.a: PUBG’s API keeps a match available for about fourteen days and then stops serving it. Match history here is that recent window rather than a career archive, and it is also why an old match cannot be opened as a replay: the data behind it is no longer there to fetch.

missingStats.a: Usually one of three things. The player has not played the current season, so there is nothing in it yet; the platform is wrong, and the account exists on another shard; or PUBG is rate-limiting us and we are serving the last good copy while that clears. The page says which of the three it is rather than showing zeroes as if they were real.

rankedRp.q: What is RP, and why is there only one number?
rankedRp.a: RP is the rating the ranked ladder is ordered by. Since Season 36 there is a single RP number per account rather than one per party type and perspective, so the tier on a profile is the tier for everything that player queues. The ranks page covers the eight tiers in order, how RP is earned and lost, and what Survivor actually requires.

limits.a: PUBG allows a fixed number of requests a minute, and everyone using this site shares it. When we reach it, a lookup serves the last good copy of that profile instead of failing, and the limit clears in about twenty seconds. Nothing is wrong with the account — waiting a moment and asking again is enough.

avatar.q: Why is there no avatar on a profile?
avatar.a: Avatars come from Steam rather than from PUBG, so they exist only for Steam accounts whose profile is public. When Steam cannot be reached or the profile is private, the page falls back to a placeholder. It says nothing about the account or its statistics.

reports.q: What is the PUBG Report tab?
reports.a: It looks up kills and deaths that were captured on Twitch streams, through the third-party pubg.report service. When a kill in a match happened to be on someone’s stream, that tab is where the clip is. It is separate from the official API, so a match can be complete here and have nothing in that tab.

favorites.a: On your device, in this browser — there are no accounts here to keep them in. Clearing site data clears them, and they will not follow you to another browser or phone. The “recently searched” list is a different thing: that one is site-wide and shows what other people have been looking up.

ranks.title: PUBG ranks explained: tiers, RP and Survivor
ranks.intro: Eight tiers, one RP number shared across party types and perspectives, and a top tier you can lose overnight — this is the ranked system as it stands on 9 September 2026, sourced to KRAFTON's patch notes and official posts, with every exception labelled.

protection.label: Tier Protection charges, Silver and up

decay.label: RP a day lost to decay at Diamond and up

ladder.heading: The eight tiers, in order
ladder.p1: PUBG: BATTLEGROUNDS has eight ranked tiers. From lowest to highest: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Crystal, Diamond, Master, Survivor.
ladder.p2: Crystal sits between Platinum and Diamond — not above Diamond. It arrived in Season 36 together with Survivor, which replaced the old Top 500 badge.
ladder.p3: Divisions run IV (lowest) to I (highest). Season 36 cut them from five to four, so there has been no division V in any tier since 11 June 2025 on PC, or 19 June 2025 on console.
ladder.p4: Master and Survivor are conventionally shown as single ranks, and PUBG's own reward tables never name a Master or Survivor division. But those tables list one row per tier for every tier, including ones that clearly have four divisions, so they prove nothing either way. KRAFTON has never published a per-tier division table.

tier.silver: Silver — the first tier where you are granted Tier Protection charges.
tier.gold: Gold — the lowest tier that earns the Ranked weapon skin and parachute skin.
tier.platinum: Platinum — the lowest tier with an animated emblem and a medal.
tier.crystal: Crystal — added in Season 36, between Platinum and Diamond.
tier.diamond: Diamond — the tier where RP decay starts if you stop playing Ranked (per the 2021 rules; see below).
tier.master: Master — a single rank, no divisions published.
tier.survivor: Survivor — the top tier. RP alone will not get you in; see below.

distribution.heading: Where players actually sit
distribution.p1: Everything above this section is what KRAFTON publishes. This part is the one thing on the page we measure ourselves: a daily random sample of ranked matches, and the current tier of fifteen players drawn from each of them.
distribution.p2: The interval beside each tier is not decoration. Players drawn from the same lobby are more alike than players drawn at random — matchmaking put them there by rating — so the sample carries less information than its raw size suggests. The intervals already account for that, which is why they are wider than the count would imply; the line under the table says how much less.
distribution.p3: A tier gets a number only when its own sample is thick enough to hold one up. Survivor is the tier this bites: a few hundred seats worldwide means a random sample of ranked lobbies may contain none at all, and a single sighting is not a measurement.
distribution.p4: Ranked resets every season, so this describes the season named below and no other. The window pools the last seven days of samples and counts each account once, at its most recent reading.
distribution.p5: One thing these shares are not: a headcount of everyone who plays. The sample is drawn from matches rather than from a list of accounts, so a player who queues twenty times a week is likelier to appear in it than one who queues twice. Read a tier's share as where a random ranked lobby seat sits, not as a census of who owns the game.
distribution.sample: Measured from {accounts} accounts across {matches} ranked matches on {platform}, {from} to {to}.
distribution.clustering: Because players in one lobby are alike, that is worth about {effective} independent readings at its tightest — which is what each interval above already allows for.

grandmaster.heading: There is no Grandmaster tier
grandmaster.p1: Grandmaster is not a PUBG rank, and it has not been one for the entire life of Ranked Mode, which launched in Update 7.2.
grandmaster.p2: It existed once, in PUBG's 2018 ranked beta — a different ladder (…Diamond, Elite, Master, Grandmaster) that was replaced by the Survival Title System in December 2018, which was itself retired when Ranked Mode launched in Update 7.2. KRAFTON's news archive no longer carries the 2018 notes, so that history is reconstructed from contemporaneous coverage rather than a first-party source.
grandmaster.p3: Guides that call Grandmaster "the top 500 players" are describing Top 500, which was awarded on top of Master rank — the emblem and nameplate went only to players at Master or above — not earned by crossing an RP threshold. Season 36 removed it and introduced Survivor in its place.

howRpMoves.heading: How RP is earned and lost
howRpMoves.p1: One RP number covers party types and perspectives. Since Season 36, tiers and RP are unified across party types (Duo/Squad) and perspectives (FPP/TPP) — no separate FPP rank to grind. Solo is not named in that sentence: it had just been removed from AS when it was written, and when AS Ranked Solo returned in Update 42.1 KRAFTON did not restate how it interacts with unified RP.
howRpMoves.p2: Placement matters more than it used to. Update 42.1 made final placement carry greater weight in the RP calculation — it does not say how much, and the formula has never been published.
howRpMoves.p3: Season 36 capped the per-match swing at −44 to +44 RP. Update 42.1 then stacked bonuses on top without restating the cap, so whether −44/+44 still bounds the final total is not something KRAFTON has said.
howRpMoves.p4: Team kills and suicides deduct RP directly since Season 36. Before that, they only reduced your kill count.
howRpMoves.p5: Your season opens with placement matches. Since Season 37 they seed from your final RP in the previous season. The full wipe to 1,500 RP in Season 36 was explicitly one-off and has not been repeated.

tierProtection.heading: Tier Protection: why you sometimes do not demote
tierProtection.p1: If a Ranked match drops your RP below your tier's minimum, Tier Protection can trigger and lock your RP at that minimum instead of demoting you.
tierProtection.p2: You are granted three charges each time you are promoted to Silver or higher, and you can hold at most three at a time.
tierProtection.p3: They also fire when RP is lost to an intentional leave, a crash or an abnormal termination — but not during placement matches, and not when you are demoted by RP decay.
tierProtection.p4: And they are a loan, not a gift: demote after burning all three and you lose an extra 50% of the RP they had protected, on top of the normal loss.
tierProtection.p5: This is the real anti-demotion mechanic. Guides describing "soft RP floors" or per-tier deduction curves are describing something PUBG has never published.
tierProtection.p6: Tier Protection does not apply to Survivor.

survivorTier.heading: Survivor: two gates, not one
survivorTier.p1: Survivor is the only tier on the current ladder KRAFTON has published an RP number for, and that number alone still will not get you in.
survivorTier.p2: Gate one: your live RP and your RP on the leaderboard must both be 3,700 or higher.
survivorTier.p3: Gate two: you must place within your region's fixed number of Survivor slots.
survivorTier.p4: Slot counts published with Season 36. PC: AS 200, SEA 100, EU 50, KAKAO 50, RU 50, NA 5, SA 5. Console: NA 50, EU 20, APAC 5, SA 5.
survivorTier.p5: KRAFTON called those numbers "subject to change based on matchmaking conditions" and has not republished them since June 2025. They are the latest published figures, which is not the same as the current ones.
survivorTier.p6: Demotion is immediate. Fall below 3,700 live RP and you drop to Master on the spot — Tier Protection does not cover Survivor. Climb back above 3,700 before the next leaderboard update and you are promoted straight back to Survivor.
survivorTier.slotsTotal: {total} seats across the PC regions listed, Kakao included — it runs on its own shard.

rpDecay.heading: RP decay, and the part nobody outside KRAFTON can answer
rpDecay.p1: At Diamond or above you must play at least one Ranked match a week. Miss it and you lose 100 RP per day until you play. That rule is from Update 13.1 (July 2021), and it was still live three years later: Update 30.1 states that Tier Protection will not activate if you are demoted due to Rank decay.
rpDecay.p2: The same patch said decay stops once RP drops below 3,000 — "when you reach Platinum I". Whether that mapping still holds is unknowable from outside. Crystal was inserted between Platinum and Diamond in Season 36 and KRAFTON has never republished either the decay floor or any tier's RP range, so 3,000 may or may not still be the Platinum I boundary.
rpDecay.p3: The last published rate is 100 RP a day. Where the floor sits now is genuinely unknown, and anyone quoting a tier for it is guessing.

update421.heading: What Update 42.1 changed
update421.p1: Update 42.1 landed on 16 June 2026 and went live on PC the next day. It is the current RP ruleset.
update421.p2: Final placement now carries greater weight in RP calculations.
update421.p3: RP losses at higher RP have been reduced, even in matches where you played well.
update421.p4: New consecutive-placement bonus: +5 RP for a Top 4 in two matches in a row, +10 RP for a Top 1 in two matches in a row. Only the highest bonus applies.
update421.p5: That streak resets at the start of a new season, and whenever a leaver penalty is applied.
update421.p6: Secret Rooms came to Ranked, and AS Ranked Solo returned after being removed in Season 36.
update421.p7: These are still the live rules. Updates 42.2 and 42.3 touched nothing about RP, tiers or divisions, and Update 43.1 changed only what a tier asks of you: in Duo and Solo, the minimum performance for Gold and above went up. The RP formula, the tier list and the divisions are untouched.

queuesAndMaps.heading: Some Ranked queues now have opening hours
queuesAndMaps.p1: Some region and mode queues now run on published UTC operating hours instead of all day. AS Solo (TPP) came back at 12:00–16:00 UTC in Update 42.1; EU Squad (TPP) was set to 13:00–24:00 UTC in Update 42.2. A queue can also go the other way and close for good: Update 43.1 discontinued TPP Duo in South America outright.
queuesAndMaps.p2: KRAFTON says the schedule "may continue to be adjusted", so check the newest patch notes before assuming your queue is live.
queuesAndMaps.p3: Season 43 Ranked map pool: Erangel, Miramar, Rondo and Taego — the same four as Season 42, each at 25%.
queuesAndMaps.p4: The Red Zone came back to Ranked in Season 36 — then Update 36.2 stopped it appearing from Phase 3 onwards on Erangel, Deston and Taego, in Ranked as well as Normal Match, so on two of the four Ranked maps the late game is Red-Zone-free. Any guide still saying the Red Zone was removed from Ranked outright is out of date — including KRAFTON's own support FAQ, which was last revised in March 2023 and still describes a six-tier ladder.
queuesAndMaps.p5: For entry to Ranked, that FAQ names a mastery requirement: Survival Mastery level 80. It is the most recent first-party figure, but it comes from the same stale article, so treat it as the best available number rather than a certainty.

seasonSchedule.heading: Season 43, and when it ends
seasonSchedule.p1: Season 43 opens on PC with the Update 43.1 maintenance on 10 September 2026: the servers come back at 08:30 UTC and the Ranked leaderboard resets with them. Console follows a week later, on 17 September. Season 42 was announced up front as a three-month season; this one was given no length at all.
seasonSchedule.p2: Update 43.1 brought three changes to Ranked and no others. In Duo and Solo the minimum performance each tier demands went up for Gold and above. South America lost its TPP Duo queue. And in the Ranked Play Point rewards, Archivist's Chests became Contender Cargo Tickets.
seasonSchedule.p3: We will not print an end date. KRAFTON has not published one for Season 43, and the PUBG API exposes no season dates at all, so every "season ends on…" date in circulation is a third-party guess being copied forward. The countdown on our own homepage is one of those guesses and says so: the date it shows is Season 42's measured 85 days added to this season's start, which is why it carries a tilde.
seasonSchedule.p4: A larger Ranked overhaul is officially in flight — announced in the 2026 roadmap, repeated in Update 42.1, no date given. Update 43.1 was not it. Expect tiers, rewards and season length to move again.

whatWeDoNotClaim.heading: What we deliberately do not claim
whatWeDoNotClaim.p1: No per-tier RP table. Survivor's 3,700 is the only tier-to-RP number KRAFTON has published for the current ladder; the one other figure that exists — the 3,000 / Platinum I anchor in the 2021 decay rules — predates Crystal and has never been restated. The "Gold: 2000–2499" style tables you find are not from any patch note. KRAFTON has never published per-tier RP bands — not in Update 7.2 when Ranked launched, not since. Every such table is third-party reconstruction copied forward.
whatWeDoNotClaim.p2: No distribution outside PC, and no RP boundary for any tier. The shares above are the Steam shard only, because that is where the sample is drawn from — console and Kakao run their own ladders and we measure neither. And a share says how many players sit in a tier, never where that tier starts in RP. What we cannot measure is left saying so in the table rather than filled in: Survivor's few hundred seats worldwide mean a week of random ranked lobbies may hold none at all.
whatWeDoNotClaim.p3: No division count for Master or Survivor. Both are conventionally shown as single ranks, but KRAFTON has never published a per-tier division table, so we do not put a number on it.
whatWeDoNotClaim.p4: No decay floor for the current ladder, for the reason above.
whatWeDoNotClaim.p5: Everything on this page is sourced to KRAFTON patch notes and official posts, and where a claim rests on anything weaker we say so on the spot. It was checked on 9 September 2026, against the Update 43.1 notes; when the rules change, this page changes.
